Watching Denzel Washington and Viola Davis together in Fences (2016) is a reminder of how powerful great acting can be.

Directed by Washington himself and based on August Wilson’s Pulitzer Prize-winning play, the film tells the story of a working-class family in 1950s Pittsburgh, exploring marriage, fatherhood, broken dreams and the emotional weight of unfulfilled ambitions.

Denzel brings an incredible amount of complexity to Troy Maxson, a deeply flawed man whose bitterness affects everyone around him. But Viola Davis is equally extraordinary as Rose, a woman who has spent years sacrificing her own dreams for her family.

The confrontation between them is one of the most emotionally devastating scenes in the film. You can feel years of love, frustration, disappointment and sacrifice coming out in a single conversation.

Both actors had previously played these characters on Broadway, and their chemistry feels incredibly natural. Viola deservedly won an Oscar for her performance.

A film that proves you don’t need elaborate sets or spectacular visuals when you have brilliant writing and two actors at the very top of their craft.
